featured_reviews.name: Ankan Singhal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited August Café recently and came away with mixed feelings.

We ordered the Mushroom Sandwich on sourdough, Paneer Tikka Panini, Pink Sauce Pasta, Veg Burger with fries, Cold Chocolate, and ended the meal with a Chocolate Cake.

Starting with the sandwiches, the Mushroom Sandwich was unfortunately quite dry and lacked the moisture and flavour you would expect. The Paneer Tikka Panini had the opposite problem, the mustard was so overpowering that it completely dominated the dish, making it taste more like a mustard sandwich than a paneer tikka panini.

The Pink Sauce Pasta was decent but nothing memorable. It wasn't bad, but it didn't stand out either.

The Veg Burger was actually the star of the meal. It was well-made, flavourful, and easily the best savoury dish we ordered. However, what left a sour taste was being charged ₹50 extra to make just a handful of fries peri-peri. Charging that amount for a full portion is understandable, but for barely six fries on the side, it felt excessive and unnecessary.

The Cold Chocolate was another disappointment—not because of the taste, which was perfectly fine, but because of the quantity. The portion felt quite small for the price being charged.

Thankfully, dessert ended the meal on a positive note. The Chocolate Cake was rich, delicious, and probably the highlight of the entire experience.

Overall, August Café has a pleasant atmosphere and some good offerings, but the food lacked consistency and some of the pricing decisions felt difficult to justify. Not a bad experience, but not one that left a strong impression either.

⭐⭐⭐ (3/5)

featured_reviews.name: Adriel Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited August Café recently and had quite a mixed but overall pleasant experience.

Starting with the Pho, this unfortunately missed the mark. It wasn’t authentic, used the wrong type of noodles, and the balance of flavours was overwhelmed by an excess of chilli oil and flakes. The Soy Chilli Noodles were also underwhelming; they lacked depth and flavour, and didn’t really stand out as a noodle dish.

On the brighter side, the Nachos were, as always, spot on, crisp, generously topped, and satisfying. The Chicken Steak with Peri Peri Sauce was another highlight, perfectly cooked, tender, and flavourful, paired beautifully with fresh, well-seasoned vegetables.

For drinks, the Elderberry Fizz with soda and basil seeds was refreshing and unique, while the Cappuccino was smooth and well-prepared.

Desserts were a strong finish to the meal; there’s a great variety to choose from. The Tiramisu Waffle was indulgent without being overly sweet, and the Ice Cream Sundae with a brownie base, ice cream, and caramel sauce was rich and satisfying.

The service deserves special mention, the staff are exceptionally polite, attentive, and quick. There’s an air-conditioned indoor section for comfort, as well as outdoor seating with a smoking area for those who prefer al fresco dining.

Not every dish hit the right note, but the warm service and pleasant ambience stood out. That said, for the meal we had and the overall experience, the pricing felt steep. While the service and setting are commendable, some dishes need refinement for the cost to feel justified.

The first thing you notice is the ambience, it’s classy, well-designed, and has that perfect café vibe where you can just sit back and relax. The crowd also adds to the experience, a nice mix of people that makes the place feel lively yet comfortable.

featured_reviews.name: Veikho Asanii
featured_reviews.review_text:
Affogato – a must-visit coffee and gelato outlet located on 17th Road in Khar West, Mumbai (near Bandra).
It looks tiny and unassuming from the roadside, but once you step inside, the stunning interior and inviting aroma of fresh coffee and gelato welcome you. The space feels like it was carved out of a smooth, swirling rock or cave — with soft curves, textured beige micro-concrete walls, ceiling, and floors inspired by gelato swirls. It's truly magical and artistic!
They offer two seating options: outdoor (without AC) and a cozy indoor AC room. The menu has a great variety of cakes, pastries, coffees, and, of course, their signature affogatos (espresso over gelato).
I tried their Cappuccino and Pain au Chocolat — both were excellent! The cappuccino came in a stylish glass cup, and the croissant was flaky, buttery, and perfectly chocolate-filled. Service was friendly and attentive.
One small downside: there's no strong AC blower at the entrance, so a few mosquitoes can be a minor nuisance (typical Mumbai evening issue in humid weather).
Overall, the experience was fantastic — highly recommended for any coffee or gelato lover in the city! ☕🍦✨

featured_reviews.name: Suhel Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tucked away in the quiet lanes of Khar, this café stands out with its bright presence and inviting, cozy interiors. The smooth textured walls, warm tones, and soft lighting create a soothing and relaxed ambiance. Even on a weekend, it wasn’t crowded, making it a perfect spot for some quiet time.

Seating is available both indoors and outdoors — though slightly limited and snug. I tried the avocado chicken, which came in a generous portion for the price and delivered beautifully on flavor. The iced mocha was made to perfection, and its pricing is pleasantly lower than most popular cafés around.

They also serve excellent gelatos, including sugar-free options sweetened with monk fruit — a thoughtful touch. Definitely planning to return to try those and the tempting quiche next time!

featured_reviews.name: Adv Surabhi Sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tried Affogato in Khar for the first time and I must say it was an absolute delight. I ordered the hazelnut affogato and it was heavenly. The blend of rich espresso poured over the creamy hazelnut gelato created the perfect balance of bitterness and sweetness. It was my first time trying an affogato and I’m so glad this was the place I chose to experience it.

The café itself has a very chic and calming vibe. It’s minimal in its design yet incredibly warm and welcoming. The use of earthy tones and the cozy setting give it a very homely feel. It’s the kind of place that instantly puts you at ease and makes you want to stay a little longer.

A big shoutout to Amit from the staff. He was genuinely sweet and courteous. We happened to be the last ones to place our order and despite the system being shut, when we expressed interest in trying the coffee gelato, Amit went out of his way to let us sample it in a small container. It was such a thoughtful gesture and honestly made our evening more special.

While everything we tried was good, the jamun sorbet truly stood out. It was refreshing, packed with flavor, and something I would go back for without a second thought.

Overall, Affogato has quickly become a new favorite. With its serene atmosphere, kind staff, and absolutely delicious offerings, I can definitely see myself visiting again and again.

featured_reviews.name: Rushabh Gundal
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a coffee and dessert enthusiast, discovering Affogato x Coffee by Javaphile was a delightful experience. This café offers a unique blend of Italian-inspired gelato and artisanal coffee, making it a must-visit for anyone who enjoys high-quality coffee and desserts.

Ambience & Design

The moment I walked in, I was captivated by the café's minimalist and modern design. The interiors have a soft, monochromatic palette inspired by swirling gelato, creating a serene and inviting atmosphere. The large, curved glass windows let in plenty of natural light, making it a perfect spot to unwind with a coffee. The outdoor seating area, surrounded by lush greenery and a calming white gravel setting, adds to the charm, making it a great place to relax and enjoy a peaceful break.

Menu Highlights

As the name suggests, Affogato x Coffee specializes in affogatos, and I couldn’t resist trying their signature affogato with Belgian Chocolate gelato. The combination of hot espresso and cold, velvety gelato was nothing short of amazing! They also have a great selection of gelato flavors, from Salted Butter Caramel to Tiramisu, all crafted using traditional Italian methods.

For those looking for something beyond affogatos, the café also offers freshly baked goods like Almond Croissants, Pain au Chocolat, and Cinnamon Rolls, which pair beautifully with their coffee. If you’re into unique coffee flavors, I highly recommend their Sea Salt Mocha or Spiced Latte—both have a perfect balance of richness and depth.

Service & Atmosphere

The staff here is friendly, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate about coffee and gelato. They are happy to guide you through the menu and help you find the perfect pairing. Another great thing is that this café is pet-friendly, making it a fantastic spot for those who want to enjoy their coffee with their furry friends.

Final Thoughts

Affogato x Coffee by Javaphile beautifully blends the art of gelato-making with specialty coffee, creating a haven for both dessert and coffee lovers. Whether you're craving a classic affogato, a scoop of creamy gelato, or a freshly brewed coffee, this place promises a memorable experience.

Would I visit again? Without a doubt!

featured_reviews.name: amin shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
you're ever around Pali Hill, Bandra West, and looking for a cozy, aesthetic spot to chill with friends or even get some work done, Ritual Daily Coffee should definitely be on your list. This café is not only known for its specialty coffee but also for its calm ambience, comfortable seating, and work-friendly vibe.

We tried their Iced Vanilla Latte, and it was as good as it looked — smooth, refreshing, and perfectly balanced in flavor. My friend went for the Biscoff Frappe, and honestly, it was a game-changer. The taste was unique and indulgent, with that Biscoff twist hitting all the right notes.

Now, let's talk food — we ordered their Rose Chicken Croffle Sandwich, and wow, this was mind-blowing. The flavor, the creativity, the texture — everything about it stood out. I can confidently say you won’t find a sandwich like this anywhere else in Mumbai. My friend and I both absolutely loved it.

We also tried the Chicken Club Sandwich, and it was packed with juicy chicken and fresh vegetables — hearty, flavorful, and satisfying. The Chicken Cilantro Quesadillas were another highlight, highly recommended by the staff, and they didn’t disappoint.

The cherry on top? Their Mango Basque Cheesecake. Soft, rich, and just the right amount of sweet — it was the perfect way to end our meal.

Service was excellent, with the staff being super friendly and helpful in recommending their best dishes. The overall experience was a solid 10/10.

Whether you're looking for a new coffee hangout, a place to work, or just craving some standout food, Ritual Daily Coffee is definitely worth the visit.

featured_reviews.name: Tanishka Rajpal
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for a warm and cozy café in Bandra West, Rituals Café is such a lovely find! From the moment you walk in, the vibe feels inviting – it has that cute, aesthetic charm that makes you want to sit down, relax, and just spend hours there. The upper deck seating is one of my favorite parts – perfect for catching up with friends, getting some work done, or even just enjoying a quiet coffee by yourself.

Coming to the food – I tried their mac & cheese and it was exactly what comfort food should taste like: creamy, cheesy, and super satisfying. The avo toast with burrata was fresh and delicious, such a perfect combination. For dessert, I went with their gluten-free chocolate cake and honestly, I couldn’t believe it was gluten-free – it was rich, fudgy, and just the right amount of sweetness. I also loved their 54% sugar-free Belgian chocolate – guilt-free but still indulgent. To finish, I had the Brazilian blueberry smoothie, which was refreshing, light, and packed with flavor.

What I really like is that everything feels thoughtfully made, and the presentation is just as good as the taste. It’s not just a café, but a spot where you can actually unwind and feel good while enjoying great food. Definitely one of those hidden gems in Bandra that I’ll be revisiting for sure. Highly recommend to anyone who loves cozy corners, comfort food, and cute café vibes! 💛

featured_reviews.review_text:
I ordered an Arrabbiata pasta and asked them to replace mushroom with another vegetable. That’s it. Not extra toppings, not some complicated off-menu request — just replacing one vegetable.

And honestly, calling that a “special customization” is ridiculous. It’s pasta, not a five-course tasting menu. Also, I have genuinely never seen mushroom in an Arrabbiata pasta on any normal menu, so acting like removing it was some massive inconvenience was bizarre from the start.

The pasta arrived completely dry, non-palatable, and barely edible, so I gave it 2 stars on the app. I didn’t even write a review initially. But apparently that was enough to trigger the owner into calling me at 11 PM to argue about why I gave a low rating.

The entire call was just constant interruption, defensiveness, and repeated lectures about how they had gone “out of their way” for me by replacing one vegetable with another. If that is considered some massive favour, then maybe don’t offer it at all.

What’s worse is the complete inability to take feedback. If you ask a customer what went wrong, at least let them speak instead of interrupting them every few seconds.

In the restaurant business, bad food is still fixable. This kind of behaviour is what actually ruins the experience. Calling customers late at night to fight over a rating is genuinely bizarre and unbelievably unprofessional.

Definitely not ordering again.

The café has such a warm and cozy vibe with a perfect blend of authentic South Indian flavours and modern café aesthetics. Every dish felt comforting, flavourful, and beautifully prepared.

We started with the Cheese Onion Uttappa which was soft, perfectly cooked, and loaded with cheese without overpowering the authentic taste. The Mutuswami Special Benne Dosa with paneer was honestly one of the highlights 🤤 crispy on the outside, buttery, rich, and filled generously with flavourful paneer stuffing.

The Ghee Roast Mushroom with Appam was another standout dish. The appams were soft and fluffy while the mushroom preparation had a beautiful spicy South Indian flavour that paired so well together. We also tried the Paneer Cheese Grilled Sandwich which was super cheesy, crisp, and comforting.

For drinks, the Chikoo Milkshake was thick, creamy, and refreshing, while the Kala Khatta Cooler from their summer specials was tangy, nostalgic, and perfect for the Mumbai heat.
Ended the meal with Mango Sheera and it was the sweetest ending possible 🤌🏻 warm, rich, and full of mango flavour without being overly sweet.

Loved the quality, presentation, ambience, and overall experience. Definitely a place I’d love visiting again for comforting South Indian food with a modern twist.

After picking up the items bought we were lucky enough to be seated on their outdoor seating area which also happens to be a smoking allowed zone.
Banana chips, sealed glass bottles were provided complementary on every table. Seating was comfortable and it was windy too. But the traffic on the road and the honking of vehicles (that are extremely closeby on the road next to the outdoor seating area) were a deterrent to a lovely experience otherwise.
There's a buzzer provided at each desk to call the staff when in need. Menu is to be scanned from the QR and hence the order placing experience was smooth. We had tried their Baked Pav Bhaji, Paneer Calzone, Filter coffee, Vietnamese iced latte, chocolate tartlet, chocolate namelaka sihi and filter kaapi misu Sihi. The Savory food items are all worth trying especially the baked pav bhaji was a melt-in-mouth and tasted fresh. The Vietnamese iced latte is skippable and filter coffee could have been better. Sihi, however, was the most anticipated item that has disappointed. The portion size was too small and the taste didn't quite impress us. Chocolate namelaka tasted more like a thickened mousse than a cheesecake. We couldn't try Papparoti as they were out of stock. Will be back to try more from their menu,possibly in the indoor seating area this time.

### **Review for Prithvi Café**
Prithvi Café is legendary for its vibe and history, but if I’m being honest, the food felt a bit overhyped. It’s a great spot to hang out, but the flavors were a hit-or-miss for me :(

So, I was leaving for out of India but just wanted to explore this cafe before leaving as I will be missing Indian food a little!
But, I kind of got disappointed with the food. To be honest the dishes I had at airport were better🥲

**The Food Breakdown:**
🌟 Egg Kheema: Just okay. It didn't quite live up to the expectations I had based on the reviews.
🌟 Butter Chicken Thali: This was a letdown. The gravy was **way too sweet**—even for Butter Chicken. It lacked that savory, spicy balance you'd expect.
🌟 Mixed Veg Paratha: One of the better items we ordered. Solid, filling, and tasted fresh.
🌟 Burger (Must Try!): The highlight of the meal. The bun isn't made of maida (refined flour), which gave it a great texture. Definitely worth a try if you want something "healthier" but tasty.
Chocolate Croissant: A decent sweet finish, but nothing groundbreaking.

**Drinks:**
We tried the Blueberry Soda and Masala Soda. Both were refreshing and served as good palate cleansers for the meal.

Go for the atmosphere and the non-maida burgers, but maybe skip the North Indian mains if you aren't a fan of sweet gravies. It's a nice place to chill, just don't expect a culinary masterpiece across the whole menu.

featured_reviews.review_text: Inspite of visiting a couple of times before, we've never shot pictures to upload in the review as this was a busy place that involved queue system to be seated. Our last visit was on a weekday afternoon and hence we got a table without a wait time. The seating is outdoor and the menu is pocket friendly and extensive. Most of their kitchen seems outdoor and causes fumes,sizzles and fragrances of multiple dishes being cooked. The dining is moderately under dhaded trees and thoroughly placed table fans. The menu and ordering are online while the bill can be paid once your are  about to leave. Service staff are busy but give you attention when needed. Our asked for extra plate/spoon have immediately been fulfilled. The orders once placed have also arrived quick to the table. We've been ordering from this place for years and hence have reordered most of our favorites to enjoy them fresh which include their paratha with dal makhani, red velvet brownie and cookies. Their sulemani chai and masala soda were well made too. No excessive sugars in the beverages that we ordered. featured_reviews.name: Mayur Aundhakar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited **Prithvi Café** and had a really good experience overall. The café has a beautiful, lively ambience with a chilled, artsy vibe — perfect for casual meetups or relaxed meals.

I tried quite a few dishes here:
🍽️ **Amritsari Paratha** – Nicely stuffed, flavorful, and served hot with curd and chutney. The taste was authentic and had a pleasant spicy punch without being overpowering.
🍝 **White Pasta** – Creamy, rich, and perfectly cooked. The sauce was smooth and mildly cheesy, though it could use a little more spice for those who like stronger flavors.
☕ **Hot Coffee & Filter Coffee Ice-Cream** – Both were excellent. The hot coffee was strong and aromatic, while the filter coffee ice-cream was a unique treat — a perfect balance of bitterness and sweetness.
🥭 **Mango Lassi** – Thick, fresh, and refreshing, with a real mango flavor. It paired well with the paratha and gave a nice desi touch to the meal.
🌯 **Chicken Roll** – Juicy, well-marinated, and wrapped in soft bread. Nicely spiced and filling; non-veg lovers will definitely enjoy this.

The **service** was polite and quick despite the crowd. **Pricing** is slightly on the higher side, but the taste and ambience justify it. The **outdoor seating** under trees gives a cozy, café-theatre vibe that’s hard to find elsewhere in Mumbai.

✅ **Overall:** Quite good experience — tasty food, soothing coffee, and vibrant atmosphere. A must-visit if you’re near Juhu, especially for coffee lovers and café enthusiasts

featured_reviews.name: Khushi Porwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Tried a few dishes at Earth Cafe and here’s my take:

🍝 Pink Sauce Pasta with Garlic Bread
Creamy, comforting, and well-balanced. The sauce had a nice richness without being too heavy, and the garlic bread was perfectly crisp. A solid crowd-pleaser.

🥑 Avocado Toasts
Fresh, chunky avocado with a good crunch from the toast. Loved the seasoning and presentation—simple but done right.

🍟 Seasoned Fries
Crispy, well-seasoned, and addictive. Perfect side to munch on while chatting.

Overall food: 8/10 — genuinely good and satisfying.

But… the space
The place feels quite congested. Tables are very close to each other, so you can easily hear nearby conversations, which takes away from the experience.

Location reality check
Getting to Juhu itself can be a task—traffic can be a bit of a mood killer.

Final verdict:
Great food, but go prepared for a slightly cramped and noisy vibe.

Aromas Cafe and Bistro - A Perfect Spot to Relax and Indulge in Juhu

Located in the vibrant area of Juhu, Aromas Cafe and Bistro offers not just a place to enjoy great food but a full experience with its aesthetic ambiance. Whether you're on a date, having a meeting, or just chilling with friends, this cafe offers the perfect vibe for any occasion. The unique wallpaper adds to the charm, making it an inviting space where you can relax with a cup of coffee or even get some work done with your laptop.

The food at Aromas is both delicious and healthy. The Avocado Smoothie Bowl and Avocado Toast stood out for their unique and fresh flavors, perfect for a nutritious start. The Chicken Burger, with its flavorful herb-garlic chicken, is ideal for those who love a healthy yet satisfying meal. Gym-goers will definitely appreciate this dish! My sister especially loved the Aromas Delight Pizza, and the Strawberry Mojito was refreshing, while the Nutella Kitkat Shake and Nutella Hot Chocolate added a sweet indulgence to the experience.

The service was fantastic, with Rizwan Sir offering excellent guidance and making sure our experience was top-notch. And the desserts? Wow! The San Sebastian Cheesecake in Biscoff flavor was a mind-blowing treat, with a taste like no other. We also tried the San Sebastian Fresh Blueberry Cheesecake, which was equally mouthwatering.

Overall, Aromas Cafe and Bistro is the perfect spot to unwind, indulge in great food, and enjoy an unforgettable atmosphere. With its mouthwatering offerings and exceptional service, it's a 10/10 experience. Highly recommended if you're in Juhu!
